ill_omen.label: Ill Omen
ill_omen.line: Each victory gathers more shadow until the omen passes.

debt.label: Debt
debt.line: The lender takes a share of each victory's gold until the debt is paid.

hunted.label: Hunted
hunted.line: Something follows your trail: the next battles each bring a wave of fresh foes. Boss maps are spared.

sworn_enemy.label: Sworn Enemy
sworn_enemy.line: The act's boss has sworn to end you, and fights with a gift from the dark until it falls.

wounded.label: Wounded
wounded.line: A wound that has not closed. They fight at a penalty until it mends.

events.title: The Old Swordmaster
events.intro: An old woman is splitting firewood with a practice sword. She hasn't missed a log. "You're staring," she says, without looking up.

choices.label: Ask her to teach
choices.hint: She looks at your sword arm, not your face.

target.reason: No one here fights with a sword, lance or axe.

outcomes.text: She drills them until dark. "Again." Again. Then, at last: "Fine."
outcomes.fallbackText: She drills them until dark, then shakes her head. "Nothing left to show you." She feeds you instead.

outcomes.text: "No." She doesn't explain. She does, however, feed you.

choices.label: Spar with her
choices.hint: Quick hands and a sharp eye will matter more than talk.

target.reason: No one here fights with a sword, lance or axe.

outcomes.text: Their blade stops at her collar. She laughs, really laughs, and fetches something wrapped in oilcloth.
outcomes.fallbackText: Their blade stops at her collar. She laughs, and fetches something wrapped in oilcloth. "I've taught you all I know."

outcomes.text: She taps their wrist. The sword drops. "Dead," she says. "Twice."
She nods at the woodpile as you go. It's very neat.

events.title: The Abandoned Armory
events.intro: The garrison left in a hurry: boots by the door, a cold pot, racks of weapons nobody came back for. Somewhere inside, a door is barred from the wrong side.

choices.label: Take from the racks
choices.hint: Plain issue, oiled and ready.

outcomes.text: Plain issue, oiled and ready. Someone kept this place.

choices.label: Search the quartermaster's desk
choices.hint: Offices keep their best things where the wrong people won't look. Or where they will.

outcomes.text: Under a loose board: a fine weapon, badly kept.
A wire, a click, and the shelf comes down on whoever was first through the door. A few coins roll out of the wreckage.

choices.label: Force the barred door
choices.hint: Barred from the wrong side. Someone wanted something kept in.

outcomes.text: Someone was still home.

effects.victoryText: The door gives way to a cellar cache nobody had touched. Weapons, and a strongbox.

choices.label: Leave it be
choices.hint: Not your garrison, not your problem.

outcomes.text: Whatever they were running from, you leave it where it is.

events.title: The Twin Altar
events.intro: Two faces cut from one stone, one toward the sunrise and one toward the dark. There are offerings before both. More before the dark one.

dark.intro: The dawn face has split down the middle and fallen. Only the dark one stands, and every offering in the temple is heaped at its feet.

choices.label: Kneel to the dark face
choices.hint: It still asks for nothing. It has never needed to.

requires.reason: The dark face has nothing left to give you.

outcomes.text: It answers before you finish. Something comes loose in you, and something else is set in its place.

choices.label: Take the offerings
choices.hint: More than there ever was. Every one of them watching you take it.

outcomes.text: The coins are cold and the dark face is not smiling now. That is worse.

choices.label: Leave the temple
choices.hint: Some doors you only need to hear close.

outcomes.text: Behind you, something puts its offerings back in order.

choices.label: Pray to the Dawn
choices.hint: It asks for a coin. It does not promise to answer, or to mean it.

requires.reason: The Dawn has nothing left to give you.

outcomes.text: Warmth on the back of the neck, like a hand.
Nothing answers. The coin is gone anyway.
Warmth on the back of the neck, like a hand. The hand does not let go.

choices.label: Pray to the face in shadow
choices.hint: It asks for nothing. That is not the same as being free.

requires.reason: The dark face has nothing left to give you.

outcomes.text: It answers at once. That should have worried you more.

choices.label: Take the offerings
choices.hint: Gold, and the dark face watching you take it.

outcomes.text: The dark face is smiling. You're almost sure it wasn't before.

events.title: The Wounded Courier
events.intro: An imperial courier sits against a milestone with an arrow through his thigh and a sealed dispatch in his fist. He watches your banner and decides not to run.

dark.intro: The courier is already dead, propped against the milestone with his hand closed on the dispatch. The seal is warm. It should not be warm.

choices.label: Read the dispatch
choices.hint: Imperial routes, and a column of names in a different hand.

outcomes.text: Routes, and beneath them a list. Yours is the last line, and the ink is still wet.

choices.label: Burn it unread
choices.hint: The seal won't like it.

outcomes.text: The seal screams, briefly. Then it is only ash, and your hand is not quite steady.

choices.label: Leave him where he sits
choices.hint: He has waited this long.

outcomes.text: You do not look back. Something behind you turns a page.

choices.label: Tend his wound
choices.hint: It costs a Vulnerary use. Gratitude is another matter.

requires.reason: You have nothing to dress his wound with.

outcomes.text: He presses a worn seer's token into your hand. "For the road. Mine's done."
He is gone by morning. So is a purse.

choices.label: Read the dispatch
choices.hint: Imperial routes, in imperial handwriting.

outcomes.text: Patrol routes, three days old. You know where they won't be.

choices.label: Sell it at the next market
choices.hint: Seals are worth gold to someone.

outcomes.text: A clerk pays well for imperial seals and asks no questions.

events.title: Deserters' Fire
events.intro: Six imperial deserters around a fire too small for them. They've seen your banner. Nobody reaches for a weapon. Yet.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.hint: They are as tired as you are.

outcomes.text: "We won't forget." Deserters always say that. They leave you their rations.

choices.label: Take their gear
choices.hint: They won't hand it over politely.

outcomes.text: They reach for their weapons after all.

effects.victoryText: Not much worth carrying, but you carry it: a decent blade and a purse of coin.

choices.label: Turn them in
choices.hint: The Empire pays for deserters, and likes them found.

outcomes.text: The bounty is paid in clean coin. It doesn't feel clean.

events.title: The Echo
events.intro: At a crossroads cairn a voice you know asks you to stop. {fallen} is here. Mostly.

choices.label: Lay them to rest
choices.hint: A proper goodbye. A church cannot revive them afterwards.

outcomes.text: You build the cairn higher. The voice thanks you, and goes.

choices.label: Ask for a last lesson
choices.hint: A last gift, and then a last goodbye.

target.reason: No one here has anything to learn from them.

outcomes.text: "Watch my feet, not my hands." Then the voice is only wind.

choices.label: "Not yet." Walk on
choices.hint: A church can still bring them back.

outcomes.text: The voice says nothing. It doesn't have to.

events.title: The Toll Bridge
events.intro: A rope bridge, a hut, and a man with a crossbow and a ledger. "Toll," he says, and names a sum. It's a lot.

dark.intro: The hut is dark and the ledger lies open. The toll-keeper sits in his chair very still, crossbow on his knee, aimed at the door. It was not the road that took him.

choices.label: Search the hut
choices.hint: Whatever he guarded is still here. So is whatever got him.

outcomes.text: Under his chair, a strongbox, and a weapon wrapped in oilcloth. He doesn't object.
The floorboards were not the only thing waiting. It stands up from the dark behind the door.

effects.victoryText: The strongbox was the bait, and the bait was real. Coin, and steel worth a second look.

choices.label: Take the ledger
choices.hint: Names, debts, and every road he ever watched. Others will want it back.

outcomes.text: Every road for a hundred miles, in a dead man's hand. Something reads over your shoulder.

choices.label: Cross in silence
choices.hint: The bridge is old. It has been counting.

outcomes.text: It holds. You stop counting how many times it creaked behind you.

choices.label: Pay the toll
choices.hint: Pay it, cross it, forget it.

outcomes.text: He writes your name in the ledger, spelled wrong.

choices.label: Bluff
choices.hint: A banner and a straight face. Luck does the rest.

outcomes.text: He looks at your banner, then at his ledger, and decides it can wait.
"Nice try." He whistles. The hut was bigger than it looked.

effects.victoryText: The ledger is yours now, and so is the strongbox behind it.

choices.label: Ford the river
choices.hint: The cheapest crossing is the coldest.

outcomes.text: Cold, fast and deeper in the middle than anyone admitted.

events.title: The Moneylender
events.intro: A gilded cart with four guards and a man in very good gloves. "Short of coin, captain? My terms are very reasonable."

choices.label: Borrow
choices.hint: Reasonable is his word, not yours. Read what you sign.

outcomes.text: He counts it out twice and smiles once.
You read the terms on the road. Then you read them again.
"Another time." He seems certain there will be one.

choices.label: Rob the cart
choices.hint: Four guards, and they were hired to be good at this.

outcomes.text: The guards were not there for show.

effects.victoryText: The man in good gloves has left his strongbox behind, and a great deal of paper.

events.title: The Drill Yard
events.intro: An abandoned drill yard: straw men, a sand pit, a rack of blunted blades. A sign reads TWO HOURS. NO EXCUSES.

dark.intro: The yard is dark and the straw men stand in ranks. Some of them have faces. The sign now reads FOUR HOURS. NO EXCUSES. NO MERCY.

choices.label: Drill until dark
choices.hint: Better by morning, and not everyone walking right.

outcomes.text: The sand runs black before they stop. Something in the straw learned with them. Someone is limping.

choices.label: Sleep in the barracks
choices.hint: The beds are made. Nobody remembers making them.

outcomes.text: Deep, dreamless and a little too long. You wake with the sun already gone.
The straw men turn their heads as you pass. None of them says a word.

choices.label: Drill until dark
choices.hint: Sore tomorrow. Better the day after.

outcomes.text: By sundown everyone is sore and nobody is slower.
Real beds. Lumpy, but real.

events.title: The Sunken Mine
events.intro: A flooded shaft, a rope ladder and three tallow torches nailed to the frame, as if someone meant to come back for them. Cold air breathes out of the dark. It smells of iron, and of something that has been sitting a long time.

choices.label: Take the ore and climb out
choices.hint: A seam of bright metal, and the rope is right there.

requires.reason: No light left to climb by.

target.reason: No weapon here can take the ore.

outcomes.text: The seam is clean. They work it into the edge by torchlight and climb out with a sharper blade.

choices.label: Go deeper
choices.hint: Every descent burns a torch. Drafts burn more.

outcomes.text: The ladder ends in a gallery of old timbers. The torchlight steadies.
A draft slides down the shaft and takes a second torch with it.

choices.label: Feel your way out
choices.hint: No light, no map, and something down here that knows the dark better than you.

tells.line: {name}: This tunnel breathes. There's a way out.
{name}: The air moves left. Left is up.

outcomes.text: Your hand finds the rope on the third try. Nobody speaks until daylight.
The rope is not where you left it. Something that lives down here has found you first.

effects.victoryText: It was guarding a purse, and the way up. You take both.

level_two.text: The gallery runs on under a low roof. A pay chest sits where its carriers dropped it, strapped shut, the lid furred with rust. The next ladder goes down.

choices.label: Take the chest and climb out
choices.hint: Heavy enough that nobody will fight you for the climb. Probably.

requires.reason: No light left to climb by.

outcomes.text: The straps give on the second try. Old imperial coin, more of it than anyone should have left down here.

choices.label: Go deeper
choices.hint: Every descent burns a torch. Drafts burn more.

outcomes.text: The ladder ends in a gallery of old timbers. The torchlight steadies.
A draft slides down the shaft and takes a second torch with it.

choices.label: Feel your way out
choices.hint: No light, no map, and something down here that knows the dark better than you.

tells.line: {name}: This tunnel breathes. There's a way out.
{name}: The air moves left. Left is up.

outcomes.text: Your hand finds the rope on the third try. Nobody speaks until daylight.
The rope is not where you left it. Something that lives down here has found you first.

effects.victoryText: It was guarding a purse, and the way up. You take both.

level_three.text: The roof opens into a hall nobody dug. A figure of black iron stands in the middle of it, one hand on a pillar, perfectly still. The air is very cold. It has been waiting for the torches.

choices.label: Face the guardian
choices.hint: It guards something. It does not look interested in conversation.

outcomes.text: It turns its head slowly, like a door.

effects.victoryText: It comes apart in plates. Behind it, on a bier of old bones, lies something that was a relic and is again.

choices.label: Leave it standing
choices.hint: Whatever it protects has kept for this long.

requires.reason: No light left to climb by.

outcomes.text: The guardian does not move. The gallery behind you is much longer going up.

choices.label: Feel your way out
choices.hint: No light, no map, and something down here that knows the dark better than you.

tells.line: {name}: This tunnel breathes. There's a way out.
{name}: The air moves left. Left is up.

outcomes.text: Your hand finds the rope on the third try. Nobody speaks until daylight.
The rope is not where you left it. Something that lives down here has found you first.

effects.victoryText: It was guarding a purse, and the way up. You take both.

events.title: The Plague Village
events.intro: Smoke from no chimney. A rag nailed to the gatepost, and behind it a village that has stopped answering. Somewhere inside, someone is coughing, and has been for a long time.

choices.label: Give your medicine
choices.hint: A Vulnerary use for strangers. The gratitude is cheaper than the dose, and slower.

requires.reason: You have no medicine left to give.

tells.line: {name}: It isn't catching. It's the well.

outcomes.text: The first dose goes down a boy's throat and stays down. A woman is crying at the door. 'More,' she says. 'Please.'
They thank you and keep coughing. A girl points, too late, at the well: green at the rim, and very still. It was never the fever.

choices.label: Loot the empty houses
choices.hint: Empty is a word you are choosing to believe.

outcomes.text: The doors are open. The rooms are not empty. You take what is on the tables and leave the people it belonged to.

choices.label: Walk around it
choices.hint: Plenty of roads go round.

outcomes.text: Four miles of nettles, and nobody to blame. The coughing follows you most of the way.

ward.text: The fever has faces now: a ring of grey children around the door, watching your pack. The first dose bought an hour. A second might buy the night.

choices.label: Give a second dose
choices.hint: It is your medicine. They are watching it leave.

requires.reason: You have no medicine left to give.

outcomes.text: The coughing eases down the street, door by door. The woman takes your hand in both of hers and does not let go for some time.

choices.label: That is all you can spare

outcomes.text: 'It's more than anyone's done.' They don't say it kindly. They don't say it unkindly either.

fever_breaks.text: By the second dose the street is quiet. Someone has put a kettle on. A woman in a healer's grey sits on the well wall, hands shaking, looking at your pack the way you look at a bill.

choices.label: Give the last dose
choices.hint: She will not forget which pack it came from.

requires.reason: You have no medicine left to give.

outcomes.text: She was the village's only healer, and she has been on her feet for nine days. 'I owe you a life,' she says, and packs her bag.
The kettle is still on when you reach the end of the street. Nobody calls after you.

events.title: The Mercenary Contract
events.intro: A free-company captain has nailed a paper to a milestone and is waiting under it, picking his teeth with a nail. 'Terms,' he says. 'Pay on delivery, penalties on failure. I'm not a sentimental man.'

choices.label: Win the next fight under par
choices.hint: Quick, or it did not happen. He keeps his own clock.

outcomes.text: He tears the paper in two and gives you your half. His half is much longer.

choices.label: Win the next fight, lose no one
choices.hint: Every name you came with, or the company starts to take an interest.

outcomes.text: He reads the names on your roll aloud, slowly, so that you will remember he did.

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: Some terms are only worth reading.

outcomes.text: 'Your funeral.' He does not sound as if he minds either way.

events.title: The Cartographer
events.intro: A woman is inking a map on the tailboard of her cart, a pen in each hand and a third behind one ear. She doesn't look up. 'Roads change,' she says. 'Mine are the ones that don't.'

choices.label: Hire her as a guide
choices.hint: She charges by the mile and knows several shortcuts. Some of them are real.

requires.reason: She walks the road a while and finds no road to add.

outcomes.text: She walks the road with you, pen scratching, and finds a path where there was not one.
outcomes.fallbackText: She walks the road with you for a mile, frowns, and shrugs. There is nothing to add. She won't take coin for nothing.

choices.label: Ask about the road ahead
choices.hint: She answers anything for free. Free answers are worth what you pay.

outcomes.text: She sketches the road ahead on your wrist in ink. Somewhere up it, a market that was not there before.
outcomes.fallbackText: She squints at the road ahead, then at you. 'It's as good as it's going to get.'

outcomes.text: She sketches a village, with a candle in its window. You will not find a village there. You will find who she told.
outcomes.fallbackText: The ink runs on your wrist. She smiles, and does not explain.

choices.label: Rob her
choices.hint: She has coin, a cart and no escort. People will remember it.

outcomes.text: She does not fight. She just watches your face the whole time, the way a mapmaker watches a coastline.

events.title: The Chained Shelf
events.intro: A scholar's shop, shuttered. In the window one book sits on a short chain, as though it might wander off. Something inside it is turning its own pages.

choices.label: Read it
choices.hint: Spellcasters only. The dark in it wants a mind that can hold a spell, and it takes rent.

target.reason: No one here can read a spell-book.

outcomes.text: The letters rearrange themselves to be read. The reader comes up for air an hour later, smiling, and a little thinner.
outcomes.fallbackText: Every page is something they already know. The book lets them go, almost politely.

choices.label: Burn it
choices.hint: Fire, and a few words said quickly.

outcomes.text: It screams, a little, in a voice like paper. When the smoke clears the air is clean for the first time in a mile.

choices.label: Sell it to a scholar
choices.hint: Someone always pays for forbidden knowledge. Usually the next buyer.

outcomes.text: A scholar in a moth-eaten gown pays, counts twice, and carries it away at arm length.

events.title: The Herald of the Hollow Sun
events.intro: A man in a grey hood stands in the road with his palms raised to a sky that has begun to dim at the edges. 'It is nearly time,' he tells you kindly. 'I only wanted to say it to someone.'

choices.label: Feed the dark
choices.hint: Power now, from something that is hungry. It remembers who fed it.

outcomes.text: The hood nods. The kneeling one stays down a long while, and rises with something new in their hands and something less in their eyes.

choices.label: Break the rite
choices.hint: He is not alone. He never is. The dark brings its own audience.

outcomes.text: The palms come down. Others step out of the ruins behind him, quietly, as if they had been waiting to be asked.

effects.victoryText: The hood falls. Beneath it, a face you almost know. The sky brightens a shade, as if someone had wiped a window.

choices.label: Listen
choices.hint: He wants to be heard, not obeyed. That may be the safest kind of man.

outcomes.text: He talks until the light is nearly gone. You understand little of it and remember all of it. Walking away, you feel strangely lighter.

events.title: The Wandering Smith
events.intro: A smith with a handcart forge has set up in the lee of a broken wall, working the bellows with one foot. 'Mend or temper,' he says, without stopping. 'Not both. I'm not made of hands.'

choices.label: Mend a worn weapon
choices.hint: Every dent, nick and rust-spot on what they carry. He charges by the visit.

outcomes.text: He sets the weapons on the anvil one by one and tuts at each. When he is done they look the way they did the day they were made.

choices.label: Temper a weapon
choices.hint: Hot work and fast hands. He says it never goes wrong. He says it fast.

target.prompt: Whose weapon goes in the fire?
target.reason: No weapon here can take the heat.

outcomes.text: The edge comes out of the quench the colour of a clean day. 'There,' he says. 'Don't thank me. Thank the fire.'
Too hot. The smith swears, quietly and at length. The weapon comes out marked, and not the way anyone wanted.
outcomes.fallbackText: Too hot. The weapon holds, but the sparks find the hand that held it.

outcomes.text: He nods at the road without breaking rhythm. The bellows sigh behind you for a long time.

events.title: The Turncoat
events.intro: A man in imperial grey sits on the verge with his boots off and his hands in plain sight. 'I'm done,' he says. 'Take me, or finish it. I'll not walk back.' He is very calm for a man who has just chosen a side.

choices.label: Take him in
choices.hint: A man who changed sides once can change them again. Or he can stay changed.

outcomes.text: He nods once, pulls his boots on, and falls in at the back. By the next fire he is sharpening someone else's knife for them.
He is gone by morning, and so is any hope of a quiet road. Torches on the ridge say your camp was counted very carefully.

choices.label: Send him off
choices.hint: Mercy is cheap on a road with this many enemies.

outcomes.text: He looks relieved, then ashamed of being relieved. He goes, and does not look back, which you decide to believe.

events.title: Old Faces
events.intro: A figure waves from a ridge, then thinks better of it and runs: the first deserter you ever let go, in a coat that no longer fits. Behind him imperial riders fan out. 'We said we wouldn't forget!' he shouts.

choices.label: Ride to his side
choices.hint: He will fight for you, if there is anyone left to ask. The riders are real.

outcomes.text: You break from the road at a run. He sees your banner and lets out a laugh that is mostly a sob.

effects.victoryText: The ridge goes quiet. Whoever is still standing is standing where they stood. 'We said we wouldn't forget,' someone says, and for once it was true.

choices.label: Toss him coin and move on
choices.hint: Not what he asked for. It might be what he needs.

outcomes.text: The purse lands in the grass. He doesn't pick it up until you are out of sight, which is the polite thing to do.

choices.label: Wave and keep walking
choices.hint: It is not your fight. It was never your fight.

outcomes.text: You walk on. Behind you he stops running, and then, a long time afterwards, so do the riders.

events.title: The Deserters' Revenge
events.intro: The deserters you sold had friends. The friends learned who sold them, and waited at a narrow place in the road with a great deal of patience and rather more rope than the occasion needs.

choices.label: Stand and fight
choices.hint: They want you to run. They have arranged the road so that you cannot.

outcomes.text: They were counting on your turning your back. You did not.

effects.victoryText: They carried everything they owned, for some reason: a deserter's savings in one place. Every coin of it was owed. You take it, since it is yours.

choices.label: Repay the bounty
choices.hint: Give back what you were paid. It will not make you friends. It might stop them being enemies.

outcomes.text: You lay the coin on a milestone. Nobody takes it until you have gone. The next time you look back the stone is bare.

choices.label: Slip away through the hills
choices.hint: A long way round, and everyone is tired by the end of it.

outcomes.text: The hills add a day and a half. Nobody follows. That is almost worse.

events.title: The Collectors
events.intro: Four men in good gloves and a clerk with an abacus wait at the ford. 'Account of the cart,' the clerk says pleasantly. 'With interest. We do try to be reasonable.'

choices.label: Pay what is owed
choices.hint: More than the cart held. They did say interest.

outcomes.text: The clerk counts it twice, ticks something, and closes the book with a sound like a coffin lid. 'A pleasure.'

choices.label: Fight the collectors
choices.hint: They have collected from better armies than yours. You will want everyone.

outcomes.text: The gloves come off. Under them are hands that have done this before.

effects.victoryText: The abacus is in pieces. The clerk, to his credit, kept counting to the end. His strongbox is yours.

choices.label: Slip away
choices.hint: They write it all down. They always write it all down.

outcomes.text: They let you go, with a bow. The clerk makes a note. The number on it is bigger than the last one.

events.title: A Bad Map
events.intro: A copy of your road is nailed to a post at the crossroads, drawn in a hand you have seen before, and a very neat one. Several of the crossings on it are wrong. In small letters at the bottom: A GIFT FROM A FRIEND.

choices.label: Trust the map
choices.hint: A gift from a friend. It would be rude to disbelieve it.

outcomes.text: The road bends where the map says it doesn't. By the time you are sure, you are in someone else's fight.
outcomes.fallbackText: You follow it a mile, wrong in all the places that do not matter. For once she was careless.

choices.label: Pay her for a true one
choices.hint: She is somewhere in the crowd. She will have set the price already.

requires.reason: The crossroads has no road a true map could add.

outcomes.text: A hand comes out of nowhere, takes the coin, and leaves a second map in your palm. It is good. It is almost kind.
outcomes.fallbackText: The hand returns your coin with a note: nothing to add. 'I am not an unfair woman.' You are not sure you believe it.

choices.label: Tear it down and walk
choices.hint: A long morning, and a short temper.

outcomes.text: You tear it down and take the road you know. It rains all afternoon, as if someone had arranged it.

events.title: A Quiet Road
events.intro: Nothing on this road but birdsong and an old well. Nobody complains.

dark.intro: The road is quiet, and the quiet is wrong. The old well has no bottom that you can see.

outcomes.text: Cold as a verdict and sweeter than it should be. Everyone feels better. Nobody looks at the water again.
The quiet follows you a mile and then thinks better of it.
A long drink and a short sleep.
You make good time.
